innerHTML: FERMIONIC COVARIANCE: A POSITIVE LOCAL LAW FOR COMPLETE PERMITTED RECORDS Private P1 construction, 2026-10-24. Version 1 after scoped native checks. The covariance dynamics and Gaussian filtering baseline are established. The scoped construction here combines exact fast quadratic closure with the separately proved quantum partial-memory record theorem. It allows arbitrary non-Gaussian preparations and CP post-event states, under the specified finite-rate and fixed-slot access contract. No claim of exact posterior compression, Gaussianization, novelty or acquired apparatus is made. 1. PHYSICAL MODEL, CONVENTIONS AND EXACT COVARIANCE EQUATION Let c_1,...,c_n obey the CAR on the full finite fermionic Fock space. Define C_ij=Tr(rho c_j^dagger c_i), dGamma(G)=sum_ij c_i^dagger G_ij c_j, so Tr(rho dGamma(G))=tr(GC). Here Tr is the Fock trace, tr the one-particle trace. Physical states and CP interventions are parity compatible. A classical hidden mode s has r possible labels; coherences between these labels are outside the classical-quantum model. For each mode and known control history the unobserved fast generator is A_s rho=-i[dGamma(h_s),rho] +gamma sum_j kappa_(s,j)(1-nu_(s,j)) D[c_j]rho +gamma sum_j kappa_(s,j)nu_(s,j) D[c_j^dagger]rho, D[L]rho=Lrho L^dagger-{L^dagger L,rho}/2, with h_s Hermitian, kappa_(s,j)>=kappa>0 and 0<=nu_(s,j)<=1. All coefficients are supplied/measured kinetic data and are well posed under the specified known causal controls. Independent fermionic reservoirs are part of the model, not derived from passive correlations or energies. With K=diag(kappa_j) and D=diag(kappa_j nu_j), CAR algebra gives C'=-i[h,C]-(gamma/2){K,C}+gamma D. (1.1) For O_ij=c_j^dagger c_i one uses D[c_k]^*O_ij=-(delta_ik+delta_jk)O_ij/2, D[c_k^dagger]^*O_ij=-(delta_ik+delta_jk)O_ij/2 +delta_ik delta_jk I. The Hamiltonian commutator supplies -i[h,C]. No Wick factorization or Gaussian initialization is used. Odd-field Heisenberg evolution is NOT asserted to be linear: for i!=k, D[c_k]^*c_i=-2n_k c_i in the ordinary Fock representation. Every proof below uses the even quadratic identity. Let M(t,u) solve M'=(-ih-gamma K/2)M, M(u,u)=I. Then C(t)=M(t,u)C(u)M(t,u)^dagger +gamma int_u^t M(t,v)D(v)M(t,v)^dagger dv. (1.2) This preserves C>=0, and the corresponding equation for I-C has source gamma(K-D)>=0. Hence the explicit positive moment body is 0<=C<=I. Conversely every matrix in this body has a gauge-invariant Gaussian realization: diagonalize C and choose independent occupations with its eigenvalues as probabilities in that orbital basis. This is a reference realization, not an assumption on the actual microscopic state. 2. THE TESTED QUADRATIC MODULE AND ITS RELAXATION All continuous channel effects, including hidden mode transitions, are R_e^s=a_e^s I+dGamma(G_e^s)>=0, sum_e R_e^s<=b(t)I. At fixed slots the CP effects are similarly quadratic and sum to I. Their classical targets and reported/coarse labels are specified. CP outputs can be non-Gaussian and correlated. Physical parity compatibility is required in addition to a positive even effect. Effects alone do not specify an instrument or its mode-transition architecture. For a Hermitian quadratic F=alpha I+dGamma(G), the Fock eigenvalues are alpha plus all subset sums of the eigenvalues of G. Therefore osc(F)=||G||_1. The adjoint fast propagator has the exact form U_(u,t)^*F=alpha_(u,t)I+dGamma(M(t,u)^dagger G M(t,u)). Since K>=kappa I, ||M(t,u)||<=exp[-a(t-u)/2], a=gamma*kappa. Thus every norm-at-most-one Hermitian quadratic satisfies osc(U_(u,t)^*F)<=2exp[-a(t-u)]. (2.1) This includes every normalized signed sum of all current rate effects, and all signed slot effects, as required by the general theorem. No mode, channel, Fock-dimension or Hamiltonian-norm factor appears in (2.1). Positivity and total-rate conditions can be checked on one-particle spectra: min spec(alpha I+dGamma(G))=alpha+sum_(lambda_j<0)lambda_j; the maximum uses positive eigenvalues. This does not provide the physical CP instrument itself. Resolved linear loss and gain maps are explicit natural examples, as are their specified coarse sums. 3. CLOSED RECORD LAW AND INITIAL DATA Retain one covariance C_s(t) per mode, evolving by (1.1) along the model's own known control record, with no slow-event conditional update. Its rates and slot probabilities are a+tr(G C_s). Positivity follows from 0<=C_s<=I. Together with the exact r-state count/slot belief filter of the general theorem this is a closed current state with rn^2+r-1 real coordinates, plus the entire initialized controller and coefficient-evaluation state. Supply the initial mode prior and the CONDITIONAL initial covariance for each occupied mode. Matching those covariances makes beta_0=0: every fast-propagated tested effect stays in the same quadratic space, so the arbitrary true conditional initial state and its covariance representative give exactly equal propagated effect expectations. Unspecified anomalous pair correlations and higher moments do not alter this statement for the number-conserving quadratic menu. All initially unused banks are initialized as well; their values matter to the implemented reference law after entry. With A(dt)=b(t)dt+(1/2)sum_j delta_(tau_j)(dt) and D(ds)=(5/4)b(s)ds+sum_j delta_(tau_j)(ds), the complete permitted-record error is E_dyn=min{1,int_(s<t)2exp[-a(t-s)]D(ds)A(dt)}. (3.1) For no slots and b<=B, a convenient expression before clipping is (5B^2/(2a))[T-(1-exp(-aT))/a]. (3.2) Instrument choices at fixed slots and known fast controls may use arbitrary causal feedback. Arbitrary record-selected continuous pulse times have not been proved. The full initialized policy must be common across comparisons. These laws predict the declared complete classical record; they do not reconstruct the conditional quantum state or approximate arbitrary final measurements. A record error epsilon gives at most 2epsilon average conditional future-record error at deterministic time under the actual past law, with no uniform rare-history posterior guarantee. 4. WHY THE EXACT CONDITIONAL COVARIANCE DOES NOT CLOSE Consider two modes and rho_A=(|00><00|+|11><11|)/2, rho_B=(|10><10|+|01><01|)/2. Both have C=I/2. A resolved loss c_1 has rate 1/2 in each, but afterward their covariances are diag(0,1) and diag(0,0). Its conditional covariance numerator contains Tr(rho c_1^dagger c_j^dagger c_i c_1), which is quartic. The no-event drift of <n_2> also differs: -Cov(n_1,n_2) is -1/4 versus +1/4. The general record theorem explicitly charges this no-event selection and the post-event disturbance; copying only the unconditional drift into an exact filter would be incorrect. An exact two-slot prediction illustrates the access dependence. Keep one classical mode, h=0, kappa_j=kappa, and nu_j=1/2 on these two sites; thus each gain/loss rate is a/2, a=gamma*kappa. At deterministic times 0<t1<t2, projectively measure occupation of site 1 and then site 2. For x,y in {-1,+1} denoting twice occupation minus one, the full two-bit laws are P_+(x,y)=(1/4)[1+xy exp(-a(t1+t2))], P_-(x,y)=(1/4)[1-xy exp(-a(t1+t2))]. Here + corresponds to rho_A and - to rho_B. Indeed L*x=-ax and L*(xy)=-2axy; the correlation at t1 is +-exp(-2at1), and the site-2 mean then decays by exp[-a(t2-t1)]. The covariance reference stays C=I/2 and predicts Q(x,y)=1/4. Hence TV(P_+,P_-)=exp[-a(t1+t2)], TV(P_+,Q)=TV(P_-,Q)=(1/2)exp[-a(t1+t2)]. The general theorem's pair allowance exp[-a(t2-t1)] safely bounds each error. Fixed positive times make the difference vanish as a grows, while t1=alpha/a, t2=beta/a with 0<alpha<beta retain a finite separation. This is an analytic finite-model prediction, not measured data or a new apparatus. The exact gauge-invariant Gaussian incumbent is stronger where its hypotheses hold. For a gauge-invariant Gaussian state, resolved loss/gain give exact updates C -> C-C e_l e_l^dagger C/C_ll, C -> C+(I-C)e_l e_l^dagger(I-C)/(1-C_ll), respectively. Gaussian-preserving propagation and instruments permit exact covariance filtering, including adaptive operations. Our approximation is not an improvement over an already exact covariance filter in that scope. Coarsening can break that scope without changing quadratic effects. Take J(rho)=(b/2)(c_1 rho c_1^dagger+c_2 rho c_2^dagger), J^*I=(b/2)(n_1+n_2)<=bI. Starting from the Gaussian |11>, an unresolved loss produces rho_B. It has <n_1n_2>=0 although its C=I/2 would give 1/4 by Gaussian factorization. Hidden mode transitions can likewise merge Gaussian branches into a non-Gaussian conditional state. The approximate law (3.1) still applies because its proof permits arbitrary physical post-event states. For n resolved losses J_j=(b/n)c_j(.)c_j^dagger the total effect is <=bI. Ordered jump words generate every square-free product of occupations, a 2^n-dimensional subspace of the exact effect space, which can be larger under hopping. Short positive-time word densities justify the limiting products; simultaneous counts are not assumed. This is a lower bound for exact unnormalized LINEAR representations across all preparations, not a fixed-error memory lower bound, a nonlinear-state bound or a simulation speedup. Distinguishing long words can be very rare. 5. LOCAL WINDOW WITHOUT A SUBCRITICAL HOPPING THRESHOLD Suppose every effect matrix is supported on a fixed port set U of a finite allowed hopping graph. Take a window W containing U. Delete hopping edges crossing W to obtain h_cut. Let B_cut include both endpoints of every deleted edge, and require d_G(U,B_cut)>=R-1>=0. This explicit convention avoids a radius off-by-one assumption. The diagonal bath remains unchanged. Assume off-diagonal row and column absolute sums of h are at most v; for Hermitian h these are the same condition. Diagonal potentials may be arbitrarily large and locally integrable. All bounds are uniform over permitted coefficient histories and modes. In the proof alone choose the full C_cut(0)=C(0). Because the cut matrices are block diagonal, the computed W-block depends ONLY on C_WW(0). No unknown exterior or cross-boundary covariance is used by the algorithm. Both full and cut covariances remain between zero and I. For theta>=0 put D_theta(x,x)=exp[-theta d_G(x,U)]. Diagonal h and K commute with D_theta; the graph-edge distance inequality and Schur norm give ||D_theta h D_theta^(-1)-h||<=v(exp(theta)-1). Hence ||D_theta M(t,u)D_theta^(-1)|| <=exp[(-a/2+v(exp(theta)-1))(t-u)]. Writing L=R-1 and q=2v/(2v+a), one obtains ||P_U M(t,u)P_(B_cut)|| <=exp[-a(t-u)/2]min{1,exp[-theta L+v(exp(theta)-1)(t-u)]}. Duhamel for the covariance difference has forcing -i[h-h_cut,C_cut]. The crossing hopping matrix h-h_cut has norm <=v and is supported on B_cut. Each of the two commutator terms requires one propagator to cross from B_cut to U; the other propagator has ordinary norm at most exp[-a(t-u)/2]. Therefore ||P_U(C-C_cut)P_U|| <=2v int_0^t exp(-a z) min{1,exp[-theta(R-1)+v(exp(theta)-1)z]}dz. Choose theta=log(1+a/(2v)) for v>0 and extend the integral to infinity: ||P_U(C-C_cut)P_U||<=min{1,(4v/a)q^(R-1)}. (5.1) For v=0 the cut error is zero. Disconnected components can be omitted. There is no boundary or port cardinality factor in this operator-norm bound. A normalized signed quadratic effect supported on U has coefficient trace norm <=2. Thus the same-record effect error is uniformly bounded by zeta_R=min{2,(8v/a)[2v/(2v+a)]^(R-1)}. (5.2) By the general theorem's second record coupling, localization adds zeta_R A([0,T])=zeta_R[int_0^T b(t)dt+J_slots/2]. (5.3) If v=gamma J_hop and a=gamma*kappa, (5.2) becomes min{2,(8J_hop/kappa)[2J_hop/(2J_hop+kappa)]^(R-1)}. Every finite hopping/reset ratio is admitted; there is no J_hop<kappa threshold. Large ratios increase the necessary window, so the resource dependence has not disappeared. This is locality of even CAR observables; it is not a statement of local qubit access after Jordan-Wigner encoding. 6. FINITE DATA, PRECISION AND COSTS The local predictor needs r physical covariance blocks C_s,WW(0) and the mode prior, not the full joint microscopic state or a full global covariance. The block includes off-diagonal coherences. Merely supplying site occupations does not meet the interface. Conditional preparation information for rare hidden modes and the controlled generator/effect/target maps must still be acquired or supplied. No covariance-matrix action is identified with a physical measurement without deriving its measurement protocol. Let C_(s,W) denote the exact cut/window solution. Let an absolutely continuous positive numerical covariance Ctilde_s in [0,I] have residual E_s=Ctilde_s'+i[h_W,Ctilde_s]+(gamma/2){K_W,Ctilde_s}-gamma D_W against the SAME known local coefficients, with ||E_s(t)||<=rho(t) and initial operator error <=delta, uniformly over relevant modes and all admitted common record histories. Duhamel and contraction give ||C_s,W-Ctilde_s||<=delta exp(-at) +int_0^t exp[-a(t-u)]rho(u)du. The corresponding normalized signed-effect error is at most twice this quantity. A complete conservative bound is therefore TV<=min{1, E_dyn_uncapped+zeta_R A([0,T]) +2 int_[0,T] [delta exp(-at) +int_0^t exp[-a(t-u)]rho(u)du] A(dt)}, (6.1) when these are the only approximations. Mode-filter, event-sampler, effect coefficient and controller errors require separate kernel certificates. Unrelated-record residual measurements or a check on one realized history do not certify (6.1). An expected allowance must specify its comparison marginal. For numerical jumps/projections at t_k, add sum_(t_k<=t) exp[-a(t-t_k)]||Ctilde(t_k+)-Ctilde(t_k-)|| to the covariance error inside the factor-two allowance. The absolutely continuous contract avoids these additional atoms. Writing m=|W|, storage is rm^2+r-1 real coordinates plus control and coefficients. Sparse h gives O(r[|E_W|m+m^2]) arithmetic per covariance right-hand-side evaluation; dense multiplication is O(rm^3). Trace evaluation charges each supplied effect, and belief propagation charges the mode-transition matrix. Piecewise constant flows can use matrix exponentials/Lyapunov integration without simulating each fast bath event, but exponentiation, dense products, every control segment and precision remain costs. No complexity independent of arbitrary input bandwidth is asserted. If maximum entry error is delta/m, operator error is at most delta; this sufficient unstructured entrywise allocation charges dimension-dependent bits. It is not a necessity for every structured operator-norm certificate. Coefficient setup, effect checks, positivity and residual certification also cost work. Generic dense spectral checks cost O(m^3), unless a stated constructive alternative supplies those guarantees. For local error tolerance epsilon_loc and Z=A([0,T])>0, a sufficient radius with v>0 is R>=1+ceil(max{0,log[(8v/a)Z/epsilon_loc]}/log[1+a/(2v)]). The window size can itself grow rapidly with radius and graph degree. Consequently independence from the total ambient size at fixed local geometry does not imply uniformly cheap inference for arbitrary graphs, vanishing damping, growing readout support or increasing observation budget. 7. PREDECESSORS, INTERPRETATION AND OPEN BOUNDARY Exact covariance closure for quadratic Hamiltonians and linear Lindblad operators, even for non-Gaussian initialization, is established: Barthel and Zhang, arXiv:2112.08344, Proposition 1. Bravyi and Koenig, arXiv:1112.2184, Sections 2, 5.1 and 6.1, supply an exact adaptive Gaussian simulation baseline and Lyapunov covariance evolution. These are not new claims here. The present consequence is the positive approximate whole-record law with arbitrary initial higher correlations and post-event non-Gaussianity, under the explicit tested relaxation and access assumptions. Historical priority for that composition remains UNKNOWN after a bounded primary comparison. The count record depends on the microscopic state through more than its covariance exactly; the finite-access law proves when that distinction is operationally small. It does not certify an exact density, exclude unknown persistent environmental variables, include arbitrary final quantum tests, or provide a diamond/ancilla norm guarantee. Generic quartic interactions, coherent slow quantum memory and critical nonlinear effects require a different module or a proved residual. An arbitrarily chosen larger Gaussian family is not a demonstrated solution to those problems. PROOF SOURCES The independent CAR/positivity/filter-obstruction proof is agents/predictive_state_obstruction_20261024/ FERMION_COVARIANCE_INTERFACE_AND_FILTER_OBSTRUCTION.txt, SHA256 745d4f865943dd3c750c8b5fceb348aa081e50d65307fc75d79fa30122d636ed. The independent weighted locality proof is agents/slow_memory_predecessors_20261024/FERMIONIC_LOCALITY_AUDIT.txt. Exact rational CAR and small-state counterexample replays are preserved beside their proofs. They check identities, not measured physical advantage. The general record theorem is separately proved and scoped-audited. Integrated root draft SHA256 91974ee2caa962ef55a145c2f11dbcbe2ac220ae40626b290eeea697f0cc23e8 received separate CAR/initial-data/precision and locality/cost checks in those two agent directories. This version incorporates the uniform-history, absolute-continuity, matrix-name and precision-contract corrections. The two-slot prediction has a separate exact proof at agents/predictive_state_obstruction_20261024/TWO_OCCUPATION_SLOT_ALGEBRA_CHECK.txt. Earlier held Green, critical, measurement and local-law sources remain unchanged.

  <=2v int_0^t exp(-a z)
                  min{1,exp[-theta(R-1)+v(exp(theta)-1)z]}dz.

norm <=2. Thus the same-record effect error is uniformly bounded by
  zeta_R=min{2,(8v/a)[2v/(2v+a)]^(R-1)}.                   (5.2)
By the general theorem's second record coupling, localization adds
  zeta_R A([0,T])=zeta_R[int_0^T b(t)dt+J_slots/2].         (5.3)

  min{2,(8J_hop/kappa)[2J_hop/(2J_hop+kappa)]^(R-1)}.
Every finite hopping/reset ratio is admitted; there is no J_hop<kappa
threshold. Large ratios increase the necessary window, so the resource
dependence has not disappeared. This is locality of even CAR observables;
it is not a statement of local qubit access after Jordan-Wigner encoding.

6. FINITE DATA, PRECISION AND COSTS

mode prior, not the full joint microscopic state or a full global covariance.
The block includes off-diagonal coherences. Merely supplying site occupations
does not meet the interface. Conditional preparation information for rare
hidden modes and the controlled generator/effect/target maps must still be
acquired or supplied. No covariance-matrix action is identified with a
physical measurement without deriving its measurement protocol.

continuous positive numerical covariance Ctilde_s in [0,I] have residual

                       +int_0^t exp[-a(t-u)]rho(u)du.

quantity. A complete conservative bound is therefore

coefficient and controller errors require separate kernel certificates.

do not certify (6.1). An expected allowance must specify its comparison
marginal. For numerical jumps/projections at t_k, add
sum_(t_k<=t) exp[-a(t-t_k)]||Ctilde(t_k+)-Ctilde(t_k-)|| to the covariance
error inside the factor-two allowance. The absolutely continuous contract
avoids these additional atoms.

coefficients. Sparse h gives O(r[|E_W|m+m^2]) arithmetic per covariance
right-hand-side evaluation; dense multiplication is O(rm^3). Trace
evaluation charges each supplied effect, and belief propagation charges
the mode-transition matrix. Piecewise constant flows can use matrix
exponentials/Lyapunov integration without simulating each fast bath event,
but exponentiation, dense products, every control segment and precision
remain costs. No complexity independent of arbitrary input bandwidth is
asserted. If maximum entry error is delta/m, operator error is at most
delta; this sufficient unstructured entrywise allocation charges
dimension-dependent bits. It is not a necessity for every structured
operator-norm certificate. Coefficient setup, effect checks, positivity and
residual certification also cost work. Generic dense spectral checks cost
O(m^3), unless a stated constructive alternative supplies those guarantees.

For local error tolerance epsilon_loc and Z=A([0,T])>0, a sufficient radius
with v>0 is

Consequently independence from the total ambient size at fixed local
geometry does not imply uniformly cheap inference for arbitrary graphs,
vanishing damping, growing readout support or increasing observation budget.

operators, even for non-Gaussian initialization, is established: Barthel and

arbitrary initial higher correlations and post-event non-Gaussianity, under

covariance exactly; the finite-access law proves when that distinction is

different module or a proved residual. An arbitrarily chosen larger
Gaussian family is not a demonstrated solution to those problems.

Private P1 construction, 2026-10-24. Version 1 after scoped native checks.

The covariance dynamics and Gaussian filtering baseline are established.
The scoped construction here combines exact fast quadratic closure with
the separately proved quantum partial-memory record theorem. It allows
arbitrary non-Gaussian preparations and CP post-event states, under the
specified finite-rate and fixed-slot access contract. No claim of exact
posterior compression, Gaussianization, novelty or acquired apparatus is made.

1. PHYSICAL MODEL, CONVENTIONS AND EXACT COVARIANCE EQUATION

Let c_1,...,c_n obey the CAR on the full finite fermionic Fock space. Define
  C_ij=Tr(rho c_j^dagger c_i),
  dGamma(G)=sum_ij c_i^dagger G_ij c_j,
so Tr(rho dGamma(G))=tr(GC). Here Tr is the Fock trace, tr the one-particle
trace. Physical states and CP interventions are parity compatible. A
classical hidden mode s has r possible labels; coherences between these
labels are outside the classical-quantum model.

For each mode and known control history the unobserved fast generator is
  A_s rho=-i[dGamma(h_s),rho]
    +gamma sum_j kappa_(s,j)(1-nu_(s,j)) D[c_j]rho
    +gamma sum_j kappa_(s,j)nu_(s,j) D[c_j^dagger]rho,
  D[L]rho=Lrho L^dagger-{L^dagger L,rho}/2,
with h_s Hermitian, kappa_(s,j)>=kappa>0 and 0<=nu_(s,j)<=1.
All coefficients are supplied/measured kinetic data and are well posed
under the specified known causal controls. Independent fermionic reservoirs
are part of the model, not derived from passive correlations or energies.

With K=diag(kappa_j) and D=diag(kappa_j nu_j), CAR algebra gives
  C'=-i[h,C]-(gamma/2){K,C}+gamma D.                        (1.1)
For O_ij=c_j^dagger c_i one uses
  D[c_k]^*O_ij=-(delta_ik+delta_jk)O_ij/2,
  D[c_k^dagger]^*O_ij=-(delta_ik+delta_jk)O_ij/2
                                      +delta_ik delta_jk I.
The Hamiltonian commutator supplies -i[h,C]. No Wick factorization or
Gaussian initialization is used. Odd-field Heisenberg evolution is NOT
asserted to be linear: for i!=k, D[c_k]^*c_i=-2n_k c_i in the ordinary
Fock representation. Every proof below uses the even quadratic identity.

Let M(t,u) solve M'=(-ih-gamma K/2)M, M(u,u)=I. Then
  C(t)=M(t,u)C(u)M(t,u)^dagger
             +gamma int_u^t M(t,v)D(v)M(t,v)^dagger dv.     (1.2)
This preserves C>=0, and the corresponding equation for I-C has source
gamma(K-D)>=0. Hence the explicit positive moment body is 0<=C<=I.
Conversely every matrix in this body has a gauge-invariant Gaussian
realization: diagonalize C and choose independent occupations with its
eigenvalues as probabilities in that orbital basis. This is a reference
realization, not an assumption on the actual microscopic state.

2. THE TESTED QUADRATIC MODULE AND ITS RELAXATION

All continuous channel effects, including hidden mode transitions, are
  R_e^s=a_e^s I+dGamma(G_e^s)>=0,        sum_e R_e^s<=b(t)I.
At fixed slots the CP effects are similarly quadratic and sum to I. Their
classical targets and reported/coarse labels are specified. CP outputs can
be non-Gaussian and correlated. Physical parity compatibility is required
in addition to a positive even effect. Effects alone do not specify an
instrument or its mode-transition architecture.

alpha plus all subset sums of the eigenvalues of G. Therefore

and all signed slot effects, as required by the general theorem. No mode,
channel, Fock-dimension or Hamiltonian-norm factor appears in (2.1).

CP instrument itself. Resolved linear loss and gain maps are explicit
natural examples, as are their specified coarse sums.
